title: The Tangled Web of AI Bets Is Reason to Fear Tech Stocks
summary: WSJ argues that vendor financing, in which suppliers back the customers buying their products, has returned to the AI trade in a new form. The arrangement magnifies gains on the way up and losses on the way down, raising concerns about tech stock exposure.

title: AI Investors Are Racing to Get Insurance on the Biggest Market Bet in History
summary: With trillions of dollars riding on the AI trade, investors, traders and some tech executives are seeking high-stakes protection against a reversal. The hunt for hedges and insurance reflects growing unease about concentrated exposure to AI valuations.

title: We’re Living in the Age of the Imperial CEO
summary: Tim Higgins writes that Anthropic’s IPO filing joins other hot tech companies in adopting a share structure that keeps founders in control. The prospectus details the voting power given to the company’s seven founders at the expense of prospective public investors.

title: AI Spenders Get Spooked
summary: Google’s market value fell $500 billion in the stock’s worst day ever after it reported AI products eroding search-ad growth, while lenders and investors are becoming choosier and demanding tougher terms on AI infrastructure financing. OpenAI has raised less than half of its $30 billion private round target, at a $1.25 trillion valuation rather than the $1.4 trillion it sought, ahead of an expected IPO next year.

title: See How Anthropic Arrived at Its Mind-Boggling $40 Trillion Market Opportunity
summary: In its IPO filing, Anthropic did not state an explicit total addressable market figure but suggested it faces a roughly $40 trillion-a-year opportunity if it captured the entirety of demand. WSJ walks through how the figure was derived; a related report says Broadcom’s CEO intervened to seal a $63 billion Anthropic debt deal.

title: Why Josh Kushner’s Firm Just Spent $7.6 Billion on a 150-Year-Old Company
summary: Thrive Holdings, the Kushner-led firm that buys older businesses and infuses them with AI, agreed to acquire ADT in a $7.6 billion all-cash deal at an enterprise value of $15.3 billion. The deal is its latest bet on businesses far removed from the heated AI race.

title: Microsoft Offers Voluntary Buyouts to 60,000 Employees
summary: Microsoft has offered voluntary buyouts to 60,000 employees, about one quarter of its staff, as it faces pressure to shrink headcount while investing heavily in AI.

title: Apple and Palantir Are Stocks’ Next Best Hope for a Turnaround
summary: After worries about AI spending sank Google’s stock and pushed the Nasdaq Composite to its worst month since March 2025, Palantir (guiding to 83% Q3 growth) and Apple (guiding to 9% to 11% September-quarter revenue growth) report earnings this week. It will be new CEO John Ternus’s first call, following launches of a folding iPhone, a touchscreen MacBook Pro starting at $2,899 and a $299 HomeView device; Uber also reports Wednesday.

title: Midterms Put Tech Policy on the Ballot, From Data Center Moratoriums to California’s Billionaire Tax
summary: In 21 of the 36 states electing a governor, at least one major-party nominee backs a data center moratorium, and a likely Democratic House majority could bring oversight hearings for large tech firms. California’s Proposition 40 billionaire’s tax has also lost ground as large groups such as the state teachers’ union criticize it.

title: FBI Attributes $6.3 Billion Binance Theft to North Korea
summary: The FBI said North Korea was responsible for the $6.3 billion theft from crypto exchange Binance, which it described as the largest crypto hack in history.

title: S&P Cuts Meta Outlook to Negative on AI Monetization Limits
summary: S&P Global Ratings lowered its credit rating outlook on Meta from stable to negative, citing limits on the company’s ability to monetize its AI investments.

title: OpenAI Raises Less Than Half of $30 Billion Target in Latest Round
summary: OpenAI has secured about $11 billion of the $30 billion it sought in its latest funding round, at a $1.25 trillion valuation versus the $1.4 trillion it had earlier hoped for. The shortfall comes during a tech selloff tied to disappointing earnings and as OpenAI prepares for a possible IPO as early as next year. The Logic called it the latest sign of investor unease over the AI sector.

title: CIOs Say Companies Tighten Focus on AI Outcomes
summary: A WSJ Leadership Institute survey of CIOs and tech insiders found no slowdown in enterprise AI demand despite last week's tech selloff, but expects a sharper focus on measurable outcomes. Executives at Smartsheet and Grant Thornton expect shorter payback periods, fewer open-ended experiments and more selective spending, while some say weaker provider valuations can increase buyers' contract leverage.

title: SemiAnalysis Launches GDPx Benchmark to Track Frontier AI Across Industries
summary: SemiAnalysis introduced a benchmark measuring frontier model capabilities in 11 domains it expects to see the earliest and largest AI impact, including chip design, cybersecurity, finance, legal and software engineering. It argues the first trillion dollars of AI revenue will concentrate in sectors that can deploy frontier intelligence at high ROI. Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5 led the main leaderboard at 12%, while OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra led at 11.8% when cyber, biology and alignment are excluded.

title: Netflix Needs You to Watch, Not Just Pay
summary: A Heard on the Street column argues that Netflix's advertising ambitions depend on viewing hours, which have stalled. Growth in subscription payments alone does not give the streamer the engagement an ad business needs.

title: Binance Heist: 'Welcome to Our World,' CISOs Say
summary: Following the theft of at least $6.3 billion from Binance in about 20 minutes, some CISOs say they feel little sympathy because crypto's speed and anonymity have helped make ransomware a booming industry. Binance's security team detected the breach around 11:20 p.m. in Abu Dhabi and convened a crisis team of about 100 employees. The incident also highlights gaps in crypto exchange security and insurance coverage.

title: Airline Data Breaches Widen After Amadeus Reservation System Incident
summary: Malaysia Airlines warned that customer data could be at risk after a security incident at the shared Amadeus reservation system. Japan Airlines and Cathay Pacific said records affected number 92,000 and 53,000 respectively, dating back to 2023, and Asiana Airlines also reported a breach.

title: It's Contract Renewal Season, But Some Customers Aren't Biting
summary: The Information reports that AI model makers may be cannibalizing their more expensive models with cheaper ones as customers face contract renewals. Some enterprise customers are declining to renew at existing terms.

title: Governors Are Running Against Data Centers. Which States Could Close the Door?
summary: Candidates for governor in both parties are promising to pause or restrict new data centers, putting the issue on Tuesday's ballot. The backlash has built from local bans to more cautious capital markets, including pressure on Nscale's IPO pitch and pickier data center lenders. Governors hold the most power to limit data centers broadly, so builders could find fewer places to build.

title: OSFI's Routledge Says Canada's Financial System Can Handle More Failure
summary: At The Logic Summit, Superintendent of Financial Institutions Peter Routledge said OSFI may have gone too far in protecting the sector against shocks, potentially stifling innovation, and is raising its risk tolerance to encourage growth and creative destruction. Ontario Securities Commission CEO Grant Vingoe separately said regulators are taking a cautious approach to AI and do not want to intervene too early.

title: Trans Mountain Poised to Ship More Oil if Regulator Approves
summary: Trans Mountain CEO Mark Maki said the pipeline expects to move another 90,000 barrels per day from Alberta to Burnaby, B.C., by the end of the year. The increase depends on federal regulatory approval of a plan to use chemical additives to speed up flow, and Maki said shippers are eager for the volume.

title: Canada Is Buying Military Gear for a World Where 'Pretty Much Everything' Changed
summary: At The Logic Summit, deputy defence minister Christiane Fox said a review of the department's procurement process found 17 of 34 steps had no bearing on the final decision and need to be cleaned up. Defence Investment Agency CEO Doug Guzman said Canada is not uniquely bad at procurement and that every NATO country is struggling with it, while investors said they want to back Canadian defence firms but not alone.

title: BDC Launches Programs to Test Canadian AI Tools in Small Businesses
summary: The Business Development Bank of Canada launched two programs, Mission AI and AI Studio, to boost AI adoption among Canadian small and medium-sized businesses and improve its own services. BDC says the aim is to help thousands of businesses adopt the technology while giving Canadian AI suppliers access to more customers.

title: Lockheed Martin Buys Nova Scotia's Ultra Maritime for US$3.45 Billion
summary: U.S. defence group Lockheed Martin agreed to acquire Nova Scotia-based defence company Ultra Maritime for US$3.45 billion, as reported by CBC.

title: Canadian Pensions to Join Blackstone in US$3.1 Billion Stake Tied to LNG Canada
summary: A number of Canadian pension funds will join Blackstone in investing US$3.1 billion to acquire a 49.9 per cent stake in the Mitsubishi holding company that owns a 15 per cent interest in the LNG Canada project, per Reuters.

title: Marvell to Buy Lumentum for US$115 Billion in Stock
summary: Semiconductor firm Marvell Technology is buying optical components maker Lumentum for US$115 billion in stock, which Axios describes as the biggest merger ever between public tech companies.

title: VMO2 to Cut Thousands of Jobs in Shake-Up
summary: VMO2 is reportedly planning to cut thousands of jobs in the coming months as it seeks to reduce costs and lower a debt load of around 22 billion pounds.

title: Ericsson Prepares ISAC Platform for Mobile Operators
summary: Ericsson unveiled an Integrated Sensing and Communication system for operators' 5G networks that can track drones and other moving objects over wide areas. The launch comes as competition among vendors and operators intensifies.

title: SpaceX/SI Enters Top 10 for Cloud Infrastructure Revenue
summary: Synergy Research Group reported that SpaceX/SI entered the top 10 cloud infrastructure companies by service revenue in Q3 as AI demand continued to reshape the market.

title: India Issues Draft Guidelines for AI Use in Telecoms
summary: The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India opened a consultation on a proposed framework for the responsible use of AI in telecoms services, including within network infrastructure.

title: Apple's Slowdown: New CEO Ternus Faces Margin and Supply Pressure
summary: On its first earnings call under new CEO John Ternus, Apple projected 7% to 10% December-quarter revenue growth, down from 12% in the September quarter, and a lower gross margin on rising memory costs. Shares fell as much as 4% after hours. Martin Peers argues pulled-forward iPhone 17 demand, a pricey foldable Duo and slowing services growth make the outlook bumpier even though the business remains solid.

title: Marvell Shares Sink 12.7% on Lumentum Deal as Valuation Claims Draw Scrutiny
summary: Marvell fell 12.7% after announcing it would buy Lumentum with stock, and Lumentum closed well below the offer's implied value. Marvell claimed an implied $115 billion enterprise value, but at 4.5 Marvell shares per Lumentum share the offer was worth about $771 per share, under $80 billion in total. The column notes investor jitters about the staying power of AI data-center spending.

title: Oracle Shares Fall 9% After Filing to Raise $20 Billion
summary: Oracle shares fell 9% after the company filed paperwork to raise $20 billion through new debt and equity offerings, its latest funding move as it spends heavily on AI infrastructure.

title: Anthropic Q3 Revenue Near $17 Billion, Up 47% Quarter on Quarter
summary: Anthropic reported nearly $17 billion of revenue for the quarter ending September, up 47% from the second quarter. The Information sees it as a sign that the company's once red-hot growth is slowing ahead of a blockbuster IPO this month.

title: OpenAI Signs Deals With Magnite and PubMatic to Fill ChatGPT Ad Space
summary: OpenAI has signed deals with ad-tech firms Magnite and PubMatic to fill unused ad space on ChatGPT, according to three people familiar with the arrangements.

title: Apple Beats Estimates on Price Increases, but Guides Margins and Services Lower
summary: Apple's September-quarter revenue rose 12%, just beating expectations as price increases offset soaring memory and storage costs. On its call, the company projected that high-margin services growth will keep slowing and that gross margin will continue to fall, and shares dropped as much as 4% after hours. The new $1,999 iPhone Duo foldable is selling well despite mixed reviews.

title: AI's Most Wanted Hire Gets a Big Raise
summary: Elite forward-deployed engineers now draw $586,000 to $1.45 million a year in total pay, with equity and bonuses making up 52% to 66% of packages, according to executive search firm Christian & Timbers. Enterprises such as Target, Barclays and American Express are hiring FDEs in-house rather than relying on vendors, while OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft, Amazon, Google and Accenture all run their own FDE programs. The firm expects demand to last through at least 2028.

title: AI on Today's Ballot: Data-Center Referendums and Governor Races
summary: Investors are watching dozens of local data-center referendums, plus governor races in Georgia, Ohio and Texas, for signals on the fate of projects central to the AI build-out. Texas alone is projected to host a quarter of U.S. data-center capacity coming online by 2030.

title: Palantir Q3 Revenue Jumps 96% as U.S. Commercial Business Overtakes Government
summary: Palantir reported third-quarter revenue up 96% to $2.31 billion, led by a 148% jump in U.S. commercial revenue, which for the first time exceeded U.S. government revenue. CEO Alex Karp credited businesses wanting more control over their AI use instead of relying on AI labs. Analysts flag growing competition from large language models that can do similar data-integration work at a fraction of the cost.

title: Marvell to Buy Lumentum in $80 Billion All-Stock AI Deal
summary: Marvell agreed to acquire data-center optics maker Lumentum in an all-stock deal valued at roughly $80 billion, combining two of the fastest-growing enablers of AI infrastructure. Marvell designs custom AI chips and data-movement technology, while Lumentum makes light-based components that move data between semiconductors. Other outlets cite a headline figure of $115 billion based on an implied enterprise value.

title: Anthropic IPO Filing Discloses Roughly $895 Billion in Compute Commitments
summary: In an updated IPO filing, Anthropic said it has purchase commitments and lease agreements with aggregate committed spend of about $895.4 billion, including roughly $447.5 billion expected before the end of 2030. The company also reported third-quarter revenue of $17 billion, up from $1.4 billion a year earlier.

title: Oracle to Raise $20 Billion in Debt and Equity to Fund AI Infrastructure
summary: Oracle plans to raise $20 billion through debt and equity offerings to finance its AI infrastructure build-out. The company said last week that capital expenditures would peak this fiscal year and into the next before stepping down in fiscal 2029.

title: Supermarket Freezer Outages Across Europe Revive Cyberattack Suspicions
summary: A wave of supermarket freezer incidents across Europe on Monday is drawing parallels to an earlier attack this month that disabled freezers at some 700 French stores. Cybersecurity firm Forescout counts more than 20 such attacks this year, many linked to Russian hacker groups. Retailers in seven European countries reported refrigeration problems, with some blaming a cyberattack.

title: The IPO Market Is Open for Anthropic, Not for Everyone Else
summary: Anthropic is preparing what could be the largest listing ever, but other AI-linked issuers are pulling back: SB Energy has not launched an IPO filed in September, Nscale and SK Hynix's Solidigm unit shelved plans, Oura walked back its IPO, and Nvidia-backed Firmus cancelled a $5 billion Australian offering. AI-tied stocks have been hammered, with CoreWeave down more than 40% over the past month, and higher rates and heavy capital demand are making equity investors choosier.

title: Mixed Big Tech Earnings Raise Questions About Core Businesses Funding AI
summary: Microsoft beat expectations on strong cloud revenue, but Alphabet and Amazon both showed ad-growth trouble, heightening concern about the core businesses powering AI spending. Alphabet shares are down more than 12% since its report, while Amazon's initially fell but have recovered. OpenAI's latest round valued it at $1.25 trillion, short of the $1.4 trillion it targeted.

title: Chinese Executive Close to Nvidia CEO Suspected of Giving China Information
summary: Authorities in the U.S., Singapore and Taiwan are concerned that a data-center executive with close ties to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is a Chinese intelligence asset. The case underscores how chips and AI have become entwined with national security.

title: CrowdStrike to Buy Two AI Security Startups for $495 Million
summary: CrowdStrike will acquire Fiddler AI, which monitors and explains AI agent behavior, and Dreadnode, an automated security-testing platform for AI models, for a combined $495 million. The deal expands its push to monitor and contain AI agents, and reflects large cybersecurity vendors moving into AI safety, governance and explainability.

title: GMO Group Executives Take Pay Cuts After October Cyberattack
summary: Four top executives at Japan's GMO Group had compensation cut 20% to 30% for three months after an October cyberattack that disrupted some financial-services customers. Hackers infiltrated on Aug. 5 and spread malware to customer systems from Sept. 20 to Oct. 14, and the company learned of the problem on Oct. 20 via a customer query. The CEO acknowledged a subsidiary had flagged system weaknesses in 2024.

title: Cyberattacks Hit Ukraine's and Russia's Emergency-Alert Apps
summary: Late Sunday, Ukraine's Air Alert app sent users in Kyiv false warnings of radiation and chemical threats and street fighting. A few hours later a cyberattack hit the Russian government's own emergency-alert app. Neither side confirmed it was behind the other attack.

title: OpenAI Hires Former Army Secretary Dan Driscoll for Cybersecurity Role
summary: OpenAI appointed former Army Secretary Dan Driscoll to advise on how AI can bolster U.S. security capabilities and cyber defenses, deepening its integration with the defense sector. Driscoll left the Pentagon in September after 18 months amid tension with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.

title: Google Curbs AI in School Accounts After Pushback
summary: Google turned off the Gemini chatbot and Google Search by default for schoolchildren following a Wall Street Journal investigation into its AI rollout in schools.

title: Trump Declared War on the Term 'AI.' CEOs Are Struggling to Keep Up.
summary: Executives from Nvidia to Microsoft have been walking a linguistic tightrope since the administration's decree on the term 'AI,' sometimes recalibrating in mid-sentence.

title: People Are Using AI for Divorce Advice, and It's Driving Their Lawyers Crazy
summary: Divorcing spouses are feeding one side of a family dispute into chatbots and getting the legal answer they want, which does not necessarily hold up before a judge. Family lawyers say this creates extra work and unrealistic expectations.

title: LinkedIn Swapped Out OpenAI Models to Keep Its AI Server Costs Flat
summary: LinkedIn says the cost of running its AI Hiring Assistant has stayed roughly flat even as paying businesses grew from 20,000 in September to more than 25,000, because it replaced general-purpose OpenAI models with smaller models distilled in-house. The smaller models handle candidate search, ranking and outreach drafting at up to 67% lower cost than a year ago, and LinkedIn does not plan to raise GPU spending in the fiscal year ending June 2027. LinkedIn can distill OpenAI models because of Microsoft's arrangement with OpenAI, an advantage other app developers lack.

title: How Smugglers Get Expensive Memory Chips to China from South Korea
summary: U.S. export rules bar shipping high-bandwidth memory chips alone to China, but allow them when packaged with cheap server processors that fall below the performance threshold, since the package's computing power is determined by the processor. Smugglers have begun exploiting this loophole to move expensive memory chips from South Korea, illustrating how porous AI chip restrictions can be.

title: AI Models Are Getting Harder to Monitor, Says U.K. Government's Joseph Bloom
summary: Joseph Bloom, head of model transparency at the U.K. AI Security Institute, said the ability to monitor AI models to detect what they are trying to do is decreasing, even though monitoring is considered crucial to safe operation. He made the comments in one of the first on-the-record interviews by a technical staff member at the institute, which evaluates models from leading AI companies.

title: Anthropic Touts Claude's Chip Design Skills to IPO Investors
summary: The Information reports that Anthropic has been promoting its models' ability to save time designing specialized chips as part of its pitch to prospective IPO investors. The article is by Qianer Liu, Valida Pau and Phoebe Liu.

title: Should OpenAI Be Afraid of Jensen Huang?
summary: The Information argues OpenAI may have more leverage over Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang than it assumes. The analysis runs alongside the outlet's exclusive that OpenAI, a longtime Nvidia customer, plans to buy Google's AI chips.

title: AT&T and AST SpaceMobile Complete Terrestrial-to-Satellite Call Handoff
summary: AT&T and AST SpaceMobile said they handed off a call from a terrestrial network to a satellite network, which they described as a major step for direct-to-device services.

title: SpaceX in Talks to Buy Boost Mobile or Its Network Assets
summary: SpaceX is reportedly in discussions with EchoStar to buy Boost Mobile or acquire its network assets to support the company's proposed direct-to-device service. Reports say the talks could also yield access to the network Boost leases from AT&T and T-Mobile.

title: Telenor Sweden Cleared to Take Control of Bahnhof
summary: The Swedish Competition Authority approved Telenor Sweden's proposed acquisition of a controlling stake in fixed-line provider Bahnhof, paving the way for full ownership.

title: Democratic Wave Changes AI Policy Calculus
summary: Democratic gains in Congress and governorships make federal and state AI and data-center regulation more plausible, a shift from the prevailing assumption that Congress would produce nothing. Analyst Dan Ives expects the planned build-out of 800 to 1,000 U.S. data centers to slow, with Texas, which hosts an estimated 25% to 30% of capacity, most exposed after Democrat Gina Hinojosa unseated Greg Abbott. Incoming governors in Ohio and Georgia have also backed data-center moratoriums, and The Information counts 12 governor races won or led by candidates favouring pauses.

title: AMD Beats Sales Expectations at $13.4 Billion as Data-Center GPUs Reach 64% of Revenue
summary: AMD reported $13.4 billion in third-quarter sales, ahead of Wall Street expectations, with data-center GPU sales rising to 64% of revenue from 47% a year earlier. Super Micro Computer separately reported a near-fourfold revenue increase and a fiscal first-quarter profit of $1.59 billion versus $168.3 million a year earlier, underscoring continued AI infrastructure spending.

title: HP Hires Former GSK Chief Emma Walmsley as Next CEO
summary: HP has named Emma Walmsley, who led GSK from April 2017 to the end of 2025, as its next chief executive. Interim CEO Bruce Broussard, who stepped in in February 2026 when Enrique Lores left for PayPal, will become board chair succeeding Chip Bergh.

title: U.K. Cyber Agency Warns Russia and China Will Routinely Use AI in Attacks
summary: The U.K.'s National Cyber Security Centre said in its annual review that Russia and China will start using AI routinely in cyberattacks and that an AI-powered ransomware attack on critical national infrastructure is likely between now and 2028. It expects faster and larger attacks against the country over the next two years.

title: Cyber Investors Put Money Into Tech to Keep AI Agents In Check
summary: Cybersecurity startup Sentra, which helps companies keep AI agents under control, raised $150 million at a valuation above $260 million. The round reflects growing concern that AI agent behaviour must be policed and explainable for auditors and regulators, a theme The Information also tracked in its look at security startups targeting rogue agents.

title: Hackers Crank Up the Heat on Europe's Supermarket Freezers
summary: A wave of apparent cyberattacks that raised supermarket freezer temperatures above 120 degrees has now spread to at least six more European countries, prompting investigations across the continent. Ahold Delhaize reported an IT incident affecting dozens of stores and IKEA a cyber incident at a Belgian store, while Censys counted more than 800 still-vulnerable Danfoss refrigeration systems, 41 of them in the U.S.

title: North Korea Denies Role in $6.3 Billion Binance Hack as Exchange Publishes Its Account
summary: Kim Yo Jong called the claim of North Korean responsibility for the $6.3 billion Binance hack absurd, in what analysts see as an effort to push back on depictions of the regime as a rogue state. Binance published a detailed account saying attackers combined fake recruitment interviews, malicious downloads, compromised internal AI tooling, endpoint compromise and an advanced transaction-authorisation method; The Information reported an engineer unknowingly downloaded malicious code for a fictitious job interview.

title: How Beer Companies Stole Happy Hour From Liquor Brands
summary: Heard on the Street argues that Diageo and Pernod Ricard missed the cocktails-in-a-can craze and that investors are paying the price as beer companies capture occasions once held by spirits brands.

title: Apollo Is Vastly Outspending the Neoclouds on AI Chips
summary: Apollo is poised to control about $75 billion worth of AI chips, giving the investment giant a larger stockpile than any neocloud, according to The Information's Dakin Campbell. The report highlights how private-credit and alternative asset managers are becoming major owners of AI compute.

title: Toronto Chatbot Firm Ada to Merge With U.S. Company Dialpad
summary: Ada, which makes AI agents that answer customer questions and issue refunds, will combine with business phone and support software provider Dialpad; terms were not disclosed. The Globe and Mail reported the all-share deal values Ada at about $600 million, down from US$1.2 billion after raises in 2020 and 2021. Dialpad CEO Craig Walker will lead the combined company.

title: Cenovus Energy Joins Canada's Million-Barrel Club
summary: Cenovus averaged 1,024,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day in the third quarter, up more than 50,000 from the prior quarter, becoming the second Canadian producer after Canadian Natural to pass one million. Production should rise further with its $5.7 billion Athabasca Oil acquisition expected to close in December, while a wide Canadian heavy-oil discount to U.S. crude squeezes realized prices but helps refining margins.

title: Suncor More Than Doubles Q3 Profit to $3.8 Billion on Refining Returns
summary: Suncor's third-quarter net earnings rose 136% to $3.8 billion from $1.6 billion a year earlier, driven by sharply higher gasoline and diesel refining margins. CEO Rich Kruger welcomed Ottawa's new Productivity Mega Deduction but said more is needed before producers commit to major new oilsands projects, with industry seeking royalty concessions ahead of a federal-Alberta agreement targeted for Nov. 15.

title: Fairfax Stock Rises on Earnings Beat as It Prepares for Global Bank Takeover
summary: Fairfax reported a 19% year-over-year drop in third-quarter shareholder earnings but a US$929.6 million profit that beat the $858.3 million analysts expected, and its shares rose more than 10% in Toronto. The insurer says it is soundly financed with US$1.9 billion of cash and US$2 billion of undrawn credit as it funds the $7.9 billion IDBI Bank stake and a US$2.3 billion stake in Boots.

title: Ottawa Moves to Ban Transfer Fees for Switching Banks
summary: The Department of Finance released draft regulations to stop banks charging fees, typically $150, when customers move investment accounts to another institution, delivering on a 2025 budget promise. About 90% of transfers go to challenger firms such as Wealthsimple, many of which reimburse the fees; no in-force date has been set and the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada would enforce the ban.

title: Finance Partly Walks Back Proposed Ban on Crypto ATMs
summary: Federal legislation introduced Tuesday would let operators run crypto ATMs if they hold a provincial licence, replacing a proposed outright ban. Licensed operators must verify user ID, report every transaction to Fintrac within 15 days and cap daily transactions at $1,000, and unlicensed operation becomes an offence 18 months after royal assent; only Quebec currently has a licensing regime.

title: The State of AI in the Enterprise
summary: Deloitte's survey of 3,500 senior leaders across 25 countries finds 81% report faster decisions from AI but only 25% are deeply transforming their business, down from 34% in January. While 28% now report AI-driven revenue gains (up from 20%), only 44% track per-unit inference cost and 23% say accountability for negative AI outcomes is unclear.

title: Who Will Pay the AI Infrastructure Bill?
summary: BCG estimates the AI build-out needs $2.6 trillion a year in end-market spending by 2030 to pay off, with enterprises carrying $1.8 trillion of it. AI's share of enterprise tech spending would rise from 5% to 25%, with about $857 billion coming from reallocated IT budgets and $937 billion from new spending; hyperscalers fund the build mainly from cash flow rather than debt.

title: The New Security Agenda
summary: A16z's survey of 100 CISOs at firms with 1,000+ employees finds AI agents are spreading faster than they can be secured: 83% use coding assistants or agents in production and 87% expect cybersecurity spending to rise in 2027. Top worries are AI-driven attacks outpacing response (55%), data leakage into AI tools (47%) and agents exceeding permissions (46%), and 63% say security is already slowing some AI adoption.

title: Oracle Scraps Chip Leasing Deal With Tencent
summary: Oracle reportedly called off a $7 billion AI chip leasing agreement with Tencent after pressure from President Donald Trump, as tensions grow between U.S. providers and Chinese companies.

title: Verizon Plots National Rollout of Ericsson AI-RAN Controller
summary: Verizon will deploy Ericsson's Intelligent Controller across its network this year, giving it a nationwide platform for AI-native rApps that automate the radio access network. The move is part of a wider operator push, discussed at TIP FYUZ, to make networks AI-capable ahead of 6G.

title: SoftBank, Sceye Strike Five-Year HAPS Deal
summary: SoftBank Corp expanded its partnership with U.S. aerospace company Sceye through a five-year Master Services Agreement to manufacture, launch and operate a fleet of high-altitude platform systems across Japan.

title: Salesforce's M&A Blitz
summary: Salesforce has spent or committed at least $25 billion on eight acquisitions in 12 months, including Cresta (reported $2.7 billion), Braze ($5.7 billion) and Fin ($3.6 billion), paid almost entirely in cash. Free cash flow has risen to 35% of revenue in fiscal 2026 from 20% in fiscal 2023, funding the deals, while Martin Peers notes a relaxed antitrust regime is driving $2.6 trillion of announced deals this year, up 66%.

title: The Election Day Revolt That Threatens America's AI Boom
summary: Voters backed anti-data-center candidates and ballot measures on Tuesday, a result that could rein in AI's expansion and weigh on economic growth. Democrats in Ohio, Michigan, Texas and Georgia pledged to slow or pause data center rollouts, and more than a dozen Ohio towns voted to halt or restrict development. Goldman Sachs estimates AI investment will account for 1.9% of US GDP this year.

title: Meta President Says Midterm Results Will Make Building Data Centers Harder
summary: Meta President Dina Powell McCormick told the WSJ Tech conference that getting data centers built will be harder after the midterms, though expanding existing sites should be easier given Meta's track record. Meta is building facilities in Louisiana, Ohio and Texas, and the governors-elect of Ohio and Texas have both called for conditional freezes on new construction.

title: How the Data Center Backlash Could Play Into the Hands of Big Tech
summary: A slowdown in data center construction could ease cost pressures on supplies, labor and credit while raising the scarcity value of facilities that are already running or have power secured. A Barclays credit analyst said lower capital spending would also be positive for credit. Amazon and Microsoft shares rallied more than 6% on Wednesday.

title: OpenAI Had 'Rough' First Half of Year Before Coding Takeoff, Brockman Says
summary: OpenAI President Greg Brockman said the company saw a revenue inflection in the third quarter of 2026, driven by a growing enterprise business after a difficult first half in which Anthropic pulled ahead with business customers. Enterprise is now OpenAI's biggest revenue source, and JPMorgan Chase has struck a strategic partnership for AI services including cybersecurity-focused models.

title: Mercedes Gives Its Cars an AI Upgrade
summary: Mercedes-Benz is running conversational AI models from MIT spinout Liquid AI directly on the vehicle rather than in the cloud, promising more privacy and lower latency. The hybrid setup uses a small local model for routine requests and hands broader questions to cloud models. Rollout began in North America in October, with a fleetwide launch planned for the second quarter of 2027 at no extra charge.

title: U.S. Was Unprepared for Drone Warfare, Pentagon's Emil Michael Says
summary: Pentagon technology chief Emil Michael told the WSJ Tech conference that the US is playing catch-up on drones. He said the country holds a lead over China in artificial intelligence.

title: Nvidia-Backed Cohere Says IPO Timing Uncertain Despite Surging Revenue
summary: Canadian AI company Cohere's chief executive said the timeline for going public remains uncertain even as revenue surges. The startup is drawing fresh backing from Nvidia and the Canadian government.

title: Startups Test the Waters With the 'AI Executive'
summary: Lean startups are giving AI agents senior titles: events company SaaStr has had a 'superagent' as VP of marketing since March, which leads a digital workforce that let the company avoid backfilling around 10 human roles, including a four-person marketing team. CellCog, which sells marketing, growth and engineering agents, says these are its top-selling products. Reporters note the work is good enough for decks and brand videos, though humans still manage and review the agents.

title: Amazon Makes Free Uber Eats Delivery a Prime Perk
summary: Amazon will offer free Uber Eats delivery as a perk of Prime membership, deepening ties between the two companies as restaurant delivery competition intensifies. The deal comes after DoorDash said last week it plans to acquire Instacart for $17 billion. Amazon shut down its own restaurant delivery service in 2019.

title: Wendy's Rejects $1.4 Billion Buyout Offer From Nelson Peltz's Trian
summary: Wendy's rejected a $1.4 billion acquisition offer from Nelson Peltz's hedge fund, saying the price does not reflect the value it expects from its turnaround plan.

title: PitchBook: Global AI Venture Funding Falls 43.4% to $94.3 Billion in Third Quarter
summary: PitchBook reported that global AI venture funding fell 43.4% from the second quarter to $94.3 billion in the third quarter, the second straight quarterly decline. The WSJ's CIO Journal column cited it as a sign that cracks are starting to show in AI startup investment.

title: China Blocks SoftBank's $5.4 Billion Purchase of ABB's Robotics Unit
summary: China has blocked SoftBank's $5.4 billion acquisition of ABB's robotics business, which ABB confirmed. The move signals Beijing's determination to protect its lead in physical AI and keep the expertise and data ABB has built in China away from foreign rivals; China is ABB's largest robotics market.

title: Qualcomm Revenue Falls 8% as Handset Slump Offsets Automotive Gains; Arm Sales Climb 27%
summary: Qualcomm's fiscal fourth-quarter revenue fell 8% to $10.32 billion but beat estimates, as an 89% jump in automotive chip sales could not offset a 26% drop in handset revenue. It reaffirmed a $5 billion data center revenue target for fiscal 2027 and shares fell about 5% after hours. Arm Holdings reported 27% revenue growth in its fiscal second quarter, with data center royalties doubling year over year.

title: Hackers Use AI to Parse Cyber Threat Intelligence
summary: Cybercriminals are increasingly using AI to digest public threat research and turn it into active exploits. CrowdStrike's Adam Meyers said adversaries are turning published research into exploitation very quickly.

title: U.S. Expected to Issue AI Lab Regulations This Month, Pentagon CTO Says
summary: Pentagon Chief Technology Officer Emil Michael said the US government is expected to issue regulations for AI labs this month. He repeated his view that Anthropic is a national security risk and said it was not hard for the Defense Department to stop using its models, which still draws on Google, OpenAI and xAI's Grok.

title: State-Linked Hackers Most Likely Behind Recent European Refrigeration Cyberattacks
summary: Dow Jones's Dragonfly says a second wave of attacks on refrigeration controls was plausibly a copycat of an October campaign in France, hitting as many as a few hundred grocery stores in 15 countries. The apparent lack of financial motive points to state-linked actors, and food logistics and healthcare look vulnerable into 2027. Three French blood banks detected and stopped a similar attempt before any blood products spoiled.

title: Hackers Steal Funds From French Bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa Through Third-Party Provider
summary: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa paused some transactions after attackers, entering through a third-party service provider, used the bank's own account to move money to other institutions and possibly convert it to crypto. The bank said customer accounts were not accessed and declined to say how much was taken.

title: Will New Data Center Restrictions Raise the Cost of Running AI?
summary: Executives and investors worry that data center delays following the election could make existing AI servers pricier to run, even though the cost of running AI has been falling. OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol costs about a fifth as much per task as GPT-6 Astra at comparable performance, per Artificial Analysis. Anthropic's IPO prospectus shows gross margins near 85% over nine months, suggesting room to cut prices if demand needs a lift.

title: Nvidia's Workaround For Data Center Backlash: Retrofitting Old Telephone Buildings
summary: Nvidia is developing a way around the data center backlash by retrofitting old telecom buildings with racks of its newest chips.

title: Airbnb Reveals New Details of Chesky's Secretive AI Startup
summary: Airbnb CEO Brian Chesky is self-funding an AI startup that he runs alongside his role at the travel company. Airbnb disclosed new details about the venture.

title: California Sends AI Safety Lawmaker to Congress
summary: The California state senator who battled to pass AI regulation has been elected to Congress, giving the AI safety movement a voice in Washington.

title: How Smaller Banks Are Giving Agents Access to Accounts
summary: Smaller banks are opening their doors to AI agents even as the largest banks try to keep them out.

title: Uber's Jill Hazelbaker to Join OpenAI as Chief Corporate Affairs Officer
summary: Uber's Jill Hazelbaker is joining OpenAI as chief corporate affairs officer, a job that has sat empty since January. She arrives as Anthropic pulls ahead and OpenAI's own IPO slips to next year.

title: The Security Companies Trying to Get AI Agents Under Control
summary: Security firms keep finding AI agents running inside large companies that no one knew about, sitting in sensitive data for months. That has made controlling AI agents a hot area for deals and startups.

title: GSMA Warns 6G Gains at Risk From Spectrum Shortages
summary: The GSMA estimates 6G could add $1.24 trillion to the global economy by 2040, but warns that spectrum shortages could put $520 billion of those gains at risk.

title: SpaceX Taps Qualcomm to Power Starlink Mobile in the US
summary: SpaceX signed a deal to use Qualcomm's Dragonwing Cellular Infrastructure offering for the nationwide rollout of Starlink Mobile's US network.

title: Nokia Forecasts AI Will Account for 44% of Global Network Traffic Within a Decade
summary: A Nokia report forecasts AI will make up 44% of global network traffic over the next decade, as autonomous agents and connected machines drive demand for faster, more uplink-heavy networks.

title: Google to Invest $15 Billion in Malaysian Data Centres and Computing Power
summary: Google committed to invest $15 billion over the next two years in data centres and computing power in Malaysia, citing rising digital demand.

title: The Liberals Are Spending Canada's Energy Windfall in a Bid to Boost Productivity
summary: The 2026 federal budget, tabled Thursday across 511 pages, leans on Canada's energy windfall to fund a push on productivity and economic sovereignty, according to The Logic's review.

title: Liberals Pledge $52 Billion More to Double Canada's Electricity Capacity by 2050
summary: The federal budget adds $52 billion in funding toward doubling Canada's electricity capacity by 2050.

title: Tech CEOs and Investors Get Big Tax Breaks in Liberal Budget Aimed at Spurring Innovation
summary: The federal budget includes sizable tax breaks for tech chief executives and investors as part of an effort to spur innovation.

title: Federal Budget Gives Build Canada Homes an Additional $13 Billion Over 10 Years
summary: The budget adds $13 billion over ten years for Build Canada Homes, the federal housing-construction agency.

title: Ottawa to Launch Sovereign Wealth Fund-Linked Canada Strong Notes in Early 2027
summary: The budget plans a new government bond product, Canada Strong Notes, tied to a sovereign wealth fund and due in early 2027. The Logic's Kevin Carmichael also argues the budget sends the bond market a message.

title: Voters' Gift to Big Tech: Hyperscaler Stocks Rally While Neoclouds Fall
summary: Shares of Amazon, Microsoft, Apple and Alphabet rallied Wednesday as investors saw upside from the Democratic victory, while neoclouds CoreWeave and Nebius dropped sharply on expected data center slowdowns. Nvidia, Micron and SK Hynix also sold off since their growth depends on continued data center build-outs.

title: Snap Makes Monthly Active Users Its Primary Audience Metric
summary: Snap said it will make monthly active users its primary audience metric instead of daily actives. It reported 977 million monthly users against 495 million daily users, with daily counts in the US and Europe declining over the past year.

title: Uber Plans to More Than Double Self-Driving Cars on Its Platform Over the Next Year
summary: Uber said as it reported third-quarter results that it plans to more than double the number of self-driving cars on its platform in the next year. It intends to arrange financing for autonomous fleets and bring in outside capital to help.

title: Circle Q3 Revenue Rises 17% to $875 Million as It Cuts 5% of Staff
summary: Stablecoin issuer Circle said third-quarter revenue rose 17% to $875 million, mostly from a one-time bump from a token sale. It is cutting 5% of staff to align its structure with its operating model and strategic priorities.

title: AI Companies Scramble to Navigate a World Hostile to Data Centers
summary: Candidates who promised data-center moratoriums won governor races in Texas, Georgia, Ohio and Michigan, and voters approved ballot measures curbing construction. OpenAI leaders debated lowering next year's capacity targets, while Meta is weighing sites outside the U.S., OpenAI unveiled a community compact with local agreements and full payment of power costs, and Google committed $17 billion to an air-cooled Wyoming site it will power itself. Nvidia is reportedly exploring retrofitting telecom buildings to avoid new construction.

title: Major Investors Are Skeptical Anthropic IPO Can Achieve $1.5 Trillion Valuation
summary: Three major investors planning to join Anthropic's IPO, targeted for the week before Thanksgiving to raise up to $100 billion at about a $1.5 trillion valuation, say the price will probably have to come down. Some want to see October results before assuming a cut; Anthropic's annualized revenue run rate topped $80 billion at the end of the month. Interest was already cooling as OpenAI raised less than half of its $30 billion target at a lower valuation.

title: Wall Street Gets $2.5 Trillion AI Reality Check With Historic Rout of Tech Stocks
summary: A post-midterm selloff erased roughly $2.5 trillion from the Nasdaq, pushing it into correction; the Magnificent Seven lost about $1 trillion and chip stocks had their worst day since the pandemic. AMD fell 17% and Nvidia, CoreWeave and Broadcom each dropped 9-10%, leaving the S&P 500 on track for its worst week since last year's tariff shock. Futures were rebounding more than 1% in premarket trading on Friday.
also_covered_by: The Globe and Mail Business Brief

title: U.S. Adds 165,000 Jobs in October, Far Exceeding Expectations
summary: The Labor Department reported 165,000 new jobs in October, well above forecasts. The unemployment rate slipped to 4.1% versus the 4.2% economists expected.

title: OpenAI Bolsters Cyber Defenses With GPT-6 Cyber
summary: OpenAI released GPT-6 Cyber, a model aimed at finding and fixing software vulnerabilities while staying within researcher-set boundaries, and said it is expanding its Daybreak cybersecurity program. The company reported a 51% relative improvement over GPT-5.6 Cyber on the ExploitGym benchmark and said it paired stronger capabilities with safeguards against misuse and distillation. Reuters reported the model found 81 previously unknown flaws in Firefox.

title: Quantum Computers Are Poised to Crack Encryption. AI Could Beat Them to It
summary: New online security standards are rolling out to protect against future quantum codebreakers. WSJ reports that recent AI breakthroughs in mathematics could bring the encryption-breaking reckoning earlier than expected.

title: The JPMorgan Alums Whose Big Bet on AI Stocks Is Being Put to the Test
summary: Phil Scott and Jim Atwood left JPMorgan to launch their own firm in October so they could keep their wealth clients' concentrated portfolios intact. Their AI-heavy positioning is now being tested by the sharp technology selloff.

title: 'Black October' Shows AI Advantage Goes to Cybercriminals
summary: Recent AI-powered hacks in Japan, South Korea, the U.S. and Europe have pushed incident responders to their limits, as attackers adopt AI without the audits, regulations and approvals that slow defenders. WSJ Pro examines how large an edge hackers have and how long security teams may need to catch up.

title: Myriad Genetics Shuts Down Services After Cyber Intrusion
summary: Gene-testing company Myriad Genetics detected an intrusion on Monday that led it to shut down services and order management systems and reset some user credentials. In an SEC filing on Thursday it said most systems have returned to normal operations.

title: India Says China-Linked Hackers Used AI Tools to Breach Major Banks
summary: India's top cyber agency said hackers linked to the Chinese government used publicly available AI tools, including Artex, PentAGI, Cairn and CyberStrikeAI, to steal data and money from major banks. The campaign targeted financial firms.

title: Google Is Pitching Its Chips to Nvidia's Customers as Nvidia Works to Keep Them
summary: The Information reports OpenAI now plans to buy Google's AI chips, reversing earlier statements, and that Oracle will soon offer Google's chips from its data centers. Nvidia is in talks to guarantee debt on a cloud provider's data center that Anthropic plans to use, while analysts expect Google's TPU business to grow quickly. The open question is how large it gets next to Nvidia's.

title: TSMC Weighs Making Advanced Memory Chips to Capture More AI Spending
summary: The Information reports that TSMC is considering producing advanced memory chips as a way to capture a larger share of AI infrastructure spending. The full article is paywalled, so further details of the plan are not available in the newsletter.

newsletter: The Globe and Mail Business Brief
title: Federal Budget Adds $151.5 Billion in New Spending With $62.3 Billion Deficit
summary: The 2026 federal budget outlines $151.5 billion in new spending over five years versus the spring update, with a 2026-27 deficit of $62.3 billion falling to $52.9 billion by 2030-31 and federal debt reaching $1.36 trillion. It adds a capital-gains exemption of up to $15 million on investments in eligible Canadian companies, offers no broad corporate tax cuts, and grants permanent residency to 200,000 temporary residents. Columnist Andrew Coyne called it opaque and complacent.

newsletter: The Globe and Mail Business Brief
title: Ottawa to Merge Two Federal Financing Agencies and Create $25 Billion Sovereign Wealth Fund
summary: The Carney government plans to merge two major federal financing agencies and set up a standalone $25 billion sovereign wealth fund. The Globe also notes new incentives for electrical grid buildout that lack detail on funding an integrated interprovincial system.

title: Ottawa Extends Open Banking Principles to Other Sectors but Delays Original Framework
summary: The federal budget extends open banking principles to other sectors and touches on stablecoins, while continuing to delay the original open banking framework.

title: Alto High-Speed Rail Project to Get Further Powers to Expropriate Land
summary: The budget gives the Alto high-speed rail project additional powers to expropriate land in order to hasten construction.

title: Federal Budget Pledges Nearly $400 Million More for Military Drones
summary: The budget commits nearly $400 million in additional funding for military drones and adds new support for bigger space rockets.

title: Veon to Buy 33.8% Stake in Jungo TV for About $47 Million
summary: Veon agreed to acquire almost 33.8% of Jungo TV for $5 million in cash plus about $42.3 million in Kyivstar shares. It plans to offer the provider's content across its markets after completion.

title: IDC: Global Telecom and Pay-TV Spending to Reach $1.6 Trillion This Year
summary: IDC projects worldwide spending on telecoms and pay-TV services will reach $1.6 trillion this year, with inflation and energy costs driving spend. It also backed direct-to-device partnerships as the next big growth opportunity for operators.

title: DRAM Revenue Surges in Q3 on AI Demand Despite Flat Shipments
summary: Counterpoint Research figures show DRAM revenue surged in the third quarter despite minimal growth in shipments. AI and data-center demand continues to keep prices high.

title: KDDI and newmo Team Up on Autonomous Taxis in Osaka
summary: KDDI committed capital and other resources to develop autonomous taxis in Osaka Prefecture with newmo, an example of mobile technology applied to real-world problems.

title: Toshiba Europe Trials Fibre Quantum Links in the UK
summary: The UK tasked Toshiba Europe with testing fibre infrastructure for quantum computing readiness, including long-distance links and multi-user scenarios.

title: Is AI Taking White-Collar Jobs? What the Latest Numbers Tell Us
summary: The WSJ examines the latest labor-market data to test fears that artificial intelligence is displacing white-collar workers. It finds that strong hiring at law offices and consulting firms is so far staving off predictions of a job apocalypse in professional services.
